sentences.en: I think that there are two different potential solutions to this problem.

sentences.en: I think one of them is to help people understand what is a reasonable amount for them to have in their savings account
sentences.zh: 我认为其中之一是帮助人们理解储蓄账户里存多少钱才算合理，

sentences.en: and to help people understand that more savings isn't always better.
sentences.zh: 并帮助人们明白，储蓄并非越多越好。

sentences.en: And the other intervention that we find is effective is to help people understand that
sentences.zh: 我们发现有效的另一种干预措施是帮助人们理解，

sentences.en: they're not depleting their savings forever.
sentences.zh: 他们并不是永远花光了储蓄。

sentences.en: They're depleting it temporarily to be used for
sentences.zh: 他们只是暂时动用它，用于

sentences.en: the specific purpose of repaying their debt.
sentences.zh: 偿还债务这一特定目的。

sentences.en: And that's a fiscally responsible thing to do.
sentences.zh: 这在财务上是负责任的做法。

sentences.en: Now, research in behavioral economics has also found that we feel differently about forking over
sentences.zh: 行为经济学的研究还发现，我们对于用现金购买东西，

sentences.en: cash to buy something as opposed to using a credit card.
sentences.zh: 与使用信用卡支付，感受是不同的。

sentences.en: Now, a dollar is a dollar.
sentences.zh: 一美元就是一美元。

sentences.en: So the
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: dollar you spend in cash ought to be the same as the dollar you put on a card, but they somehow
sentences.zh: 你用现金花的钱应该和你在信用卡上花的钱是一样的，但它们不知为何

sentences.en: feel different.
sentences.zh: 感觉不同。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if this is another example of mental accounting at work and how we
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否是“心理账户”在起作用的另一个例子，以及我们

sentences.en: might be able to take advantage of this.
sentences.zh: 该如何利用这一点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's also interesting research
sentences.zh: 确实有很有趣的研究

sentences.en: looking at, this is called sort of the pain of payment.
sentences.zh: 探讨了这一点，这被称为“支付痛苦”。

sentences.en: And so when you're parting with your
sentences.zh: 当你掏出

sentences.en: cash, it's very salient to you how costly it is, exactly how much money you're parting with.
sentences.zh: 现金时，你会非常清楚地感受到代价，确切地知道你付出了多少钱。

sentences.en: On the credit card, it's a lot easier to spend money actually without even realizing what the
sentences.zh: 而使用信用卡时，人们更容易在甚至没有意识到

sentences.en: total cost is.
sentences.zh: 总成本的情况下花钱。

sentences.en: So if you go to the supermarket and you're paying with cash, you probably know
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你去超市用现金支付，你可能知道

sentences.en: how much you spent.
sentences.zh: 你花了多少钱。

sentences.en: If you're paying with a credit card, you might not.
sentences.zh: 如果你用信用卡支付，你可能就不知道了。

sentences.en: And there are other aspects of
sentences.zh: 支付过程中的其他方面

sentences.en: the payment process that can be harder or easier and more or less painful as a result.
sentences.zh: 也会导致支付变得更难或更容易，痛苦程度也各不相同。

sentences.en: And so
sentences.zh: 所以，

sentences.en: more recent forms of payment, things like Apple Pay or these mobile payments are going to be
sentences.zh: 更现代的支付方式，比如Apple Pay或这些移动支付，

sentences.en: even lower in pain of payment.
sentences.zh: 带来的支付痛苦会更低。

sentences.en: So it's going to be even easier and less painful to spend money
sentences.zh: 因此，随着支付机制变得越来越抽象，

sentences.en: as the payment mechanism becomes less concrete.
sentences.zh: 花钱会变得更容易，也更不痛苦。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, is it possible that if you actually want to get a better grip on your
sentences.zh: 我想知道，如果你真的想更好地控制自己的

sentences.en: spending, to actually use cash more often?
sentences.zh: 支出，是否可以更频繁地使用现金？

sentences.en: I mean, it seems strange to say, but it feels like that actually might be sensible advice.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这听起来可能很奇怪，但感觉这确实是一个明智的建议。

sentences.en: I think absolutely you can use cash.
sentences.zh: 我认为绝对可以使用现金。

sentences.en: I think the world has moved so far over in terms of internet purchases that I think that
sentences.zh: 我认为世界在互联网购物方面已经走得太远了，所以我认为

sentences.en: there are other recommendations that actually would be relevant as well.
sentences.zh: 还有其他建议也同样适用。

sentences.en: So things like just not having your computer save your credit card information, for example, that might not be as far over as using cash,
sentences.zh: 比如不要让电脑保存你的信用卡信息，这可能不像使用现金那么极端，

sentences.en: but within the confines of still maintaining the convenience of being able to use your credit card in cases where it's not feasible to use cash.
sentences.zh: 但在无法使用现金的情况下，依然能保持使用信用卡带来的便利。

sentences.en: You know, for me, I think there's just there's no reason to have the payments be so easy that you can buy something without without even necessarily realizing you're buying it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，对我来说，我认为没有理由让支付变得如此简单，以至于你可以在甚至没有意识到自己在购买的情况下就买下东西。

sentences.en: So, Abby, you've spent all these years thinking about mental accounting and the foibles that we humans have.
sentences.zh: Abby，你花了这么多年研究心理账户和我们人类的弱点。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, has it changed the way you yourself make financial decisions, the way you yourself save and spend money?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，这是否改变了你自己做财务决策的方式，以及你存钱和花钱的方式？

sentences.en: One of the ways that I think it's changed my thinking is in generally making me pretty confident that I should be tracking my expenses more closely than I do.
sentences.zh: 我认为它改变我思维方式的一点是，让我更加确信我应该比现在更密切地追踪我的支出。

sentences.en: Another way that it's affected my thinking in the opposite direction is that it's made me realize how important it is both to save money on big expenses,
sentences.zh: 它影响我思维的另一个方面是，它让我意识到在大的开支上省钱是多么重要，

sentences.en: where there's the ability through a single decision to save a lot of money, but also when thinking about very small purchases that are quite routine,
sentences.zh: 因为通过一个决定就能省下一大笔钱，但同时，在考虑那些非常琐碎的日常小额消费时，

sentences.en: something that I might buy at the supermarket.
sentences.zh: 比如我在超市买的东西。

sentences.en: You know, if I really want to buy the organic strawberries instead of the regular strawberries, even though they cost an extra 50 cents,
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我真的想买有机草莓而不是普通草莓，即使它们贵了50美分，

sentences.en: this is something that I think I'm increasingly allowing myself to do and trying not to feel too bad about it.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我越来越允许自己这样做，并尽量不去为此感到太难过。

sentences.en: And this comes back to this idea of context effects where you can think about what's the percent of the total purchase that you're saving versus what is the absolute amount that you're saving.
sentences.zh: 这又回到了“情境效应”的概念，你可以考虑你节省的是总购买额的百分比，还是你节省的绝对金额。

sentences.en: And so I'm trying to save a lot of money on bigger purchases rather than trying to save a little bit of money on smaller purchases that actually matter a lot for how happy you are going through your day.
sentences.zh: 所以我尽量在大的开支上省钱，而不是在那些对你日常生活幸福感影响很大的小额消费上省那一点点钱。

sentences.en: So basically, don't sweat the small stuff.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，不要为小事烦恼。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 莱舍尔日。

sentences.en: In 2017, after a long battle with Alzheimer's, Lesher's mother Stephanie passed
sentences.zh: 2017年，在与阿尔茨海默病长期抗争后，Lesher的母亲Stephanie去世

sentences.en: away.
sentences.zh: 了。

sentences.en: But years before that, before anyone knew about her disease, Stephanie was living a pretty
sentences.zh: 但在那之前的几年，在任何人知道她患病之前，Stephanie过着相当

sentences.en: normal life.
sentences.zh: 正常的生活。

sentences.en: She would often make the 45-minute drive to visit Lesher and her two granddaughters
sentences.zh: 她经常开车45分钟去探望Lesher和她的两个孙女，

sentences.en: in another part of Connecticut.
sentences.zh: 她们住在康涅狄格州的另一个地方。

sentences.en: It was a route she had driven hundreds of times.
sentences.zh: 那是一条她开过数百次的路线。

sentences.en: But one day, when she was supposed to come to Lesher's house, Stephanie didn't show up.
sentences.zh: 但有一天，当她本该去Lesher家时，Stephanie没有出现。

sentences.en: By the time she realized that she was lost, it turns out she was in Rhode Island.
sentences.zh: 当她意识到自己迷路时，发现自己已经在罗德岛州了。

sentences.en: So when she realized she pulled over to a gas station, and I think she approached a young man at one of the pumps,
sentences.zh: 所以当她意识到这一点时，她把车停在了一个加油站，我想她走向了加油泵旁的一位年轻人，

sentences.en: and she must have explained to him that she was loSt.
sentences.zh: 她一定向他解释说她迷路了。

sentences.en: And I think probably in the conversation that she had with this stranger,
sentences.zh: 我想大概在与这位陌生人的交谈中，

sentences.en: He must have realized that my mother suffered from memory loss.
sentences.zh: 他一定意识到我母亲患有记忆力减退。

sentences.en: So this perfect stranger did something I think is pretty remarkable.
sentences.zh: 所以这位素不相识的陌生人做了一件我认为非常了不起的事情。

sentences.en: You know, he could have done nothing at all.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他本可以什么都不做。

sentences.en: But instead, he told my mother to go ahead and get back in her car and follow him.
sentences.zh: 但他却告诉我的母亲回到车里跟着他走。

sentences.en: And so he drove from wherever they were in the state of Rhode Island,
sentences.zh: 于是他从他们在罗德岛州的那个地方开车，

sentences.en: all the way into the middle of Connecticut, to central Connecticut, where she lived.
sentences.zh: 一直开到她居住的康涅狄格州中部。

sentences.en: And he kept her in his rearview mirror the entire time.
sentences.zh: 他全程都让她的车出现在他的后视镜里。

sentences.en: And my mother was, you know, a pretty slow and careful driver.
sentences.zh: 而我母亲，你知道，开车相当慢且谨慎。

sentences.en: So I'm guessing that that trip one way probably took him easily an hour and a half just to
sentences.zh: 所以我猜那趟单程旅行他可能花了足足一个半小时，

sentences.en: get her back home.
sentences.zh: 才把我母亲送回家。

sentences.en: My mother did show me a slip of paper that this man had given her.
sentences.zh: 我母亲确实给我看了一张那个人给她的纸条，

sentences.en: and all it said was his first name, Jason, and there was a 401 telephone number, a Rhode Island
sentences.zh: 上面只写了他的名字Jason，还有一个401开头的电话号码，是罗德岛的

sentences.en: exchange.
sentences.zh: 区号。

sentences.en: And eventually that slip of paper disappeared.
sentences.zh: 后来那张纸条不见了。

sentences.en: I don't know if, you know, if my
sentences.zh: 我不知道，你知道，是我

sentences.en: mother threw it away or if I, in cleaning out her house eventually, maybe, maybe I somehow misplaced
sentences.zh: 母亲把它扔了，还是我在清理她房子时，可能，可能我不小心弄丢了

sentences.en: it.
sentences.zh: 它。

sentences.en: So if I knew who Jason was, and if I could, if you were standing in front of me today,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我知道Jason是谁，如果我能，如果你今天站在我面前，

sentences.en: I would say thank you.
sentences.zh: 我会说谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you for saving my mother's life.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你救了我母亲的命。

sentences.en: Thank you for preserving her dignity that day.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你那天维护了她的尊严。

sentences.en: Thank you, Jason.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，Jason。
